issues.body: In promote_one(), only the first --remove-label write is checked. Every triage delta edit and the promotion comment ignores returncode, after which the function logs and returns "promoted". If adding status:ready (or another required triage label) fails after trust:untrusted has been removed, the issue has crossed the trust boundary but is left partially triaged; poll() reports success, main() exits 0, and later cron runs cannot retry because fetch_quarantined() no longer selects it. The test only covers failure of the first write, so it cannot catch this partial-commit path.
issues.fix_hint: Check every required post-removal gh write and propagate failure. Since removing quarantine makes the issue disappear from future polls, implement a fail-closed recovery/rollback strategy (for example, restore trust:untrusted if any required triage edit fails, and report failure) and add a self-test that injects failure into a post-unquarantine label edit, asserting a nonzero outcome and a recoverable/quarantined final state. Handle comment failure according to an explicit policy, without claiming full success if the notice is required.
issues.title: Post-unquarantine write failures are silently treated as successful promotion

verdict.summary: The paginated fetch and revision-bound approval checks are well covered, but the extracted driver still reports a promotion as successful after only the quarantine-label removal succeeds. Because all subsequent triage-label and comment writes discard their return codes, a transient failure can permanently leave an issue outside quarantine without the required trusted triage state, while the cron exits green and will never retry that issue. This is a major correctness and trust-workflow gap, and the self-test does not exercise it.
